content.title: About
content.content: Ketchup is a thick sauce made from tomato paste, vinegar, sugar and spices. It is widely used as a condiment for fast food, fries, burgers and many other dishes. Ketchup has a sweet‑tart flavor and a bright red color.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first tomato ketchup appeared in the United States in the late 19th century.
The word “ketchup” derives from the Chinese sauce “kê-chiap”, originally based on fermented seafood.
In 1906 Heinz patented a recipe that became the standard for most modern versions.
Ketchup is often used as a benchmark for spiciness in culinary competitions.
Some countries sell sugar‑free ketchup, using sweeteners instead of sugar.

items.title: Source of lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes in ketchup are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that supports heart health.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Ketchup provides vitamin C, which helps strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Unlike many sauces, ketchup typically contains very little fat.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: The vinegar in ketchup can help improve digestion.

items.title: Enhances flavor without extra salt
items.content: Its sweet‑tart profile allows reduction of added salt in dishes.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Many commercial ketchups contain a significant amount of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and increase diabetes risk.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Vinegar and added salt make ketchup a source of sodium, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or the spices used.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands use preservatives and sweeteners that can cause sensitivity in susceptible people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve ketchup with french fries, burgers, hot dogs, eggs, omelets, and even meat dishes. It can be used as a base for barbecue sauce, marinades, or added to salad dressings.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ketchup in the refrigerator after opening, in a tightly sealed container. Unopened bottles can be kept at room temperature for several months, but once opened the shelf life drops to 1‑2 months.
